title: Jacob, father of R' Nachman
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: According to the testimony of his son Rav Nachman, his father was among the scribes of Mar Shmuel’s judges, as explained in [Bava Metzia 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.16b.9).

He was indeed a great man, as we find in [Beitzah 26b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.26b.2): Rabbah bar Rav Huna expounded, and Rav Nachman said to him, “My father taught it.” Hyman likewise cites Zevachim 53a: a tanna recited these before R' Nachman, who said to him, “Thus my father told me.” We have already explained in the entry on R' Nachman that an unqualified “R' Nachman” is bar Jacob, even according to Rashi’s view.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Bava Metzia 16b:9 in the William Davidson Hebrew edition explicitly names Rav Nachman and says that his father was one of the scribes of Mar Shmuel’s judges. “Scribes” may also be rendered “clerks”; it does not add a separately described court. The heading’s abbreviated title and the later unqualified name remain R'. Jacob’s identification as the father is Hyman’s; that paragraph does not itself name the father.

Hyman’s printed Beitzah כו. gives 26a, but the matching account is at 26b:2 in the checked Davidson edition. It explicitly names Rabbah bar Rav Huna and Rav Nachman; the prior Bar Chana guess is withdrawn. Rashi’s Vilna commentary there glosses אבא תני with על אביו קאמר, “he is speaking about his father,” supporting “My father taught it,” not “Abba, teach it.” The cited Zevachim exchange was not located in the checked 53a, 53b or 52b, so its locator and wording remain Hyman’s report. A tanna here is a reciter of a teaching. No recipient of the final pronoun or separate historical identity is supplied. The concluding first-person cross-reference remains Hyman’s claim.
